low-level-design/solid-principles--inter.explanation: Overcorrecting into dozens of one-method interfaces, when a small cohesive group of methods always travels together anyway, trades one problem for a different kind of clutter.

low-level-design/solid-principles--inter.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Interface Segregation Principle?

“If an implementer has to fake, ignore, or throw on part of an interface, that interface is bundling more than one ____ actually needs — split it along those lines.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--inter.explanation: If an implementer has to fake, ignore, or throw on part of an interface, that interface is bundling more than one client actually needs — split it along those lines.

low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Dependency Inversion Principle?

“High-level modules shouldn't depend on low-level modules directly — both should depend on an ____ in between, so a change to one detail never has to ripple up into business logic that shouldn't care about it.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.explanation: High-level modules shouldn't depend on low-level modules directly — both should depend on an abstraction in between, so a change to one detail never has to ripple up into business logic that shouldn't care about it.

low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Dependency Inversion Principle?

“DIP says the high-level code should depend on an ____ it defines in its own terms, and the low-level mechanism should implement that ____ — not the other way around, where high-level logic is written against a specific low-level class's API.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.explanation: DIP says the high-level code should depend on an interface it defines in its own terms, and the low-level mechanism should implement that interface — not the other way around, where high-level logic is written against a specific low-level class's API.

low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Dependency Inversion Principle?

“An OrderService that directly writes ____ inside its own constructor is coupled to that one concrete class — swapping storage, or testing OrderService without a real database, means editing OrderService itself.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.explanation: An OrderService that directly writes new MySQLDatabase() inside its own constructor is coupled to that one concrete class — swapping storage, or testing OrderService without a real database, means editing OrderService itself.

low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Dependency Inversion Principle?

“Conflating DIP with “always use a ____ framework” overstates it — DIP is the principle (depend on abstractions), and a DI framework is just one common mechanism for satisfying it, not a requirement.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.explanation: Conflating DIP with “always use a dependency injection framework” overstates it — DIP is the principle (depend on abstractions), and a DI framework is just one common mechanism for satisfying it, not a requirement.

low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Dependency Inversion Principle?

“Depend on an interface your own code defines, not on a specific low-level ____ — the mechanism for wiring it together is a separate, later decision.”
low-level-design/solid-principles--depen.explanation: Depend on an interface your own code defines, not on a specific low-level class — the mechanism for wiring it together is a separate, later decision.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Class Diagrams?

“A ____ shows a design's static structure — the classes that exist, their attributes and methods, and the relationships between them — giving visual notation to the vocabulary this course already built up in words.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.explanation: A class diagram shows a design's static structure — the classes that exist, their attributes and methods, and the relationships between them — giving visual notation to the vocabulary this course already built up in words.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Class Diagrams?

“Relationships between classes are drawn as lines, distinguished by the same vocabulary covered earlier — association, aggregation, ____, dependency — so the diagram communicates not just which classes exist, but exactly how they're coupled.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.explanation: Relationships between classes are drawn as lines, distinguished by the same vocabulary covered earlier — association, aggregation, composition, dependency — so the diagram communicates not just which classes exist, but exactly how they're coupled.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Class Diagrams?

“A two-class diagram for a tiny library slice: a Book box listing title and author as attributes and no methods of its own, and a Library box listing a books collection as an attribute and ____ as a method, connected to Book by an aggregation line — the library holds books, but a book's existence doesn't depend on any one library holding it.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.explanation: A two-class diagram for a tiny library slice: a Book box listing title and author as attributes and no methods of its own, and a Library box listing a books collection as an attribute and addBook() as a method, connected to Book by an aggregation line — the library holds books, but a book's existence doesn't depend on any one library holding it.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Class Diagrams?

“Drawing a class diagram with only names and no attributes or ____ loses most of the information a class diagram actually exists to convey.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.explanation: Drawing a class diagram with only names and no attributes or methods loses most of the information a class diagram actually exists to convey.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Class Diagrams?

“A class ____ earns its keep by showing attributes, methods, and relationships together — a box with just a name is barely more useful than a bullet list.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--class-dia.explanation: A class diagram earns its keep by showing attributes, methods, and relationships together — a box with just a name is barely more useful than a bullet list.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Sequence Diagrams?

“Where a class diagram shows static structure, a ____ shows dynamic behavior — the order that messages pass between specific objects for one concrete scenario, over time.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.explanation: Where a class diagram shows static structure, a sequence diagram shows dynamic behavior — the order that messages pass between specific objects for one concrete scenario, over time.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Sequence Diagrams?

“The diagram makes the order of these calls — and which call is waiting on which — explicit in a way a ____ never could.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.explanation: The diagram makes the order of these calls — and which call is waiting on which — explicit in a way a class diagram never could.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Sequence Diagrams?

“For a “place an order” scenario: ____ calls OrderService.placeOrder(), which calls Inventory.reserve(), waits for its response, then calls PaymentService.charge(), waits for that response, and finally returns a confirmation back to the ____.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.explanation: For a “place an order” scenario: Customer calls OrderService.placeOrder(), which calls Inventory.reserve(), waits for its response, then calls PaymentService.charge(), waits for that response, and finally returns a confirmation back to the Customer.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Sequence Diagrams?

“Trying to use one ____ diagram to describe every possible path through a system, instead of one concrete scenario, turns it into an unreadable tangle.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.explanation: Trying to use one sequence diagram to describe every possible path through a system, instead of one concrete scenario, turns it into an unreadable tangle.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Sequence Diagrams?

“A class ____ tells you the pieces exist; a sequence ____ tells you the order they actually talk in for one specific scenario.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--sequence-.explanation: A class diagram tells you the pieces exist; a sequence diagram tells you the order they actually talk in for one specific scenario.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from State Diagrams?

“A ____ is worth drawing for objects whose behavior genuinely depends on “what mode am I in right now” — an order, a traffic light, a media player — showing every state it can be in and exactly which events move it between them.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.explanation: A state diagram is worth drawing for objects whose behavior genuinely depends on “what mode am I in right now” — an order, a traffic light, a media player — showing every state it can be in and exactly which events move it between them.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from State Diagrams?

“States are drawn as boxes or rounded shapes; ____ are labeled arrows showing which event moves the object from one state to another.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.explanation: States are drawn as boxes or rounded shapes; transitions are labeled arrows showing which event moves the object from one state to another.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from State Diagrams?

“An order's states: Placed → Paid → Shipped → ____, with a Cancelled state reachable from Placed or Paid — but deliberately not from Shipped or ____, since a shipped order can't simply be cancelled without a separate returns process.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.explanation: An order's states: Placed → Paid → Shipped → Delivered, with a Cancelled state reachable from Placed or Paid — but deliberately not from Shipped or Delivered, since a shipped order can't simply be cancelled without a separate returns process.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from State Diagrams?

“Missing an invalid ____ — allowing “Delivered” to move back to “Cancelled” simply because nobody thought to exclude it — is the exact class of bug this diagram exists to prevent.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.explanation: Missing an invalid transition — allowing “Delivered” to move back to “Cancelled” simply because nobody thought to exclude it — is the exact class of bug this diagram exists to prevent.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from State Diagrams?

“A missing arrow in a state ____ is a design decision, not an oversight — it's often the most important information the ____ carries.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--state-dia.explanation: A missing arrow in a state diagram is a design decision, not an oversight — it's often the most important information the diagram carries.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Use Case Diagrams?

“A ____ shows who can do what with a system, at the highest level of abstraction UML offers — closer to a scoping tool than a design tool, and usually the very first diagram drawn, before any class exists.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.explanation: A use case diagram shows who can do what with a system, at the highest level of abstraction UML offers — closer to a scoping tool than a design tool, and usually the very first diagram drawn, before any class exists.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Use Case Diagrams?

“A ____ diagram deliberately says nothing about how the system achieves any of it — that's what class and sequence diagrams are for, once scope is agreed on.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.explanation: A use case diagram deliberately says nothing about how the system achieves any of it — that's what class and sequence diagrams are for, once scope is agreed on.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Use Case Diagrams?

“A library system has two actors: Member and ____.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.explanation: A library system has two actors: Member and Librarian.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Use Case Diagrams?

“Listing ____-level operations, like “validate ISBN checksum,” as if they were use cases confuses a user-meaningful goal with an internal step toward one.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.explanation: Listing implementation-level operations, like “validate ISBN checksum,” as if they were use cases confuses a user-meaningful goal with an internal step toward one.

low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Use Case Diagrams?

“A use case diagram fixes scope — who needs to do what — before any class or ____ gets to decide how.”
low-level-design/uml-modeling--use-case-.explanation: A use case diagram fixes scope — who needs to do what — before any class or sequence diagram gets to decide how.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Singleton Pattern?

“____ ensures a class has exactly one instance and gives every caller the same shared access point to it — the right tool for a genuinely shared, expensive resource, and an easy pattern to reach for too often.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.explanation: Singleton ensures a class has exactly one instance and gives every caller the same shared access point to it — the right tool for a genuinely shared, expensive resource, and an easy pattern to reach for too often.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Singleton Pattern?

“It fits things like a configuration manager or a ____, where having two separate instances would mean two different, inconsistent views of the same resource.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.explanation: It fits things like a configuration manager or a connection pool, where having two separate instances would mean two different, inconsistent views of the same resource.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Singleton Pattern?

“A Logger class with a private constructor and a static ____ method: the first call constructs the one instance and every later call — from any part of the application — returns that same object, so all log output goes through one consistently-configured logger rather than several independently-configured ones.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.explanation: A Logger class with a private constructor and a static getInstance() method: the first call constructs the one instance and every later call — from any part of the application — returns that same object, so all log output goes through one consistently-configured logger rather than several independently-configured ones.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Singleton Pattern?

“Reaching for Singleton as a substitute for proper ____ turns it into hidden global state — any class can silently depend on it without that dependency ever appearing in a constructor, which makes testing and reasoning about the code harder.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.explanation: Reaching for Singleton as a substitute for proper dependency injection turns it into hidden global state — any class can silently depend on it without that dependency ever appearing in a constructor, which makes testing and reasoning about the code harder.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Singleton Pattern?

“Singleton is right for a genuinely shared resource, not a convenient way to avoid passing a dependency through a ____ — and it needs real thought about concurrent first-time creation.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--si.explanation: Singleton is right for a genuinely shared resource, not a convenient way to avoid passing a dependency through a constructor — and it needs real thought about concurrent first-time creation.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Factory Method Pattern?

“Factory Method defines an interface for creating an object, but lets ____ decide which concrete class actually gets instantiated — calling code depends on an abstract product type, never a specific class.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.explanation: Factory Method defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses decide which concrete class actually gets instantiated — calling code depends on an abstract product type, never a specific class.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Factory Method Pattern?

“An abstract Creator class declares a factory method that returns some abstract Product type; each concrete Creator subclass ____ that method to return its own matching concrete Product subclass.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.explanation: An abstract Creator class declares a factory method that returns some abstract Product type; each concrete Creator subclass overrides that method to return its own matching concrete Product subclass.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Factory Method Pattern?

“A NotificationFactory with ____ and SmsNotificationFactory subclasses, each overriding createNotification() to return an EmailNotification or SmsNotification respectively.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.explanation: A NotificationFactory with EmailNotificationFactory and SmsNotificationFactory subclasses, each overriding createNotification() to return an EmailNotification or SmsNotification respectively.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Factory Method Pattern?

“Using Factory Method where a plain ____ call would do — with no subclass logic that actually varies — adds a hierarchy for no real benefit.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.explanation: Using Factory Method where a plain constructor call would do — with no subclass logic that actually varies — adds a hierarchy for no real benefit.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Factory Method Pattern?

“Factory Method lets subclasses choose which concrete product gets built — useful only when that choice genuinely varies by ____, not as a default way to construct objects.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--fa.explanation: Factory Method lets subclasses choose which concrete product gets built — useful only when that choice genuinely varies by subclass, not as a default way to construct objects.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Abstract Factory Pattern?

“Abstract Factory produces a whole family of related objects through one ____, without specifying their concrete classes — one call gets you a matched set, not just one product.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.explanation: Abstract Factory produces a whole family of related objects through one interface, without specifying their concrete classes — one call gets you a matched set, not just one product.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Abstract Factory Pattern?

“Where Factory Method returns one product via subclassing, Abstract Factory returns several related products via composition — a single factory object exposes methods like createButton() and ____, and a concrete factory implementation guarantees every product it returns belongs to the same family, so they're never accidentally mismatched.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.explanation: Where Factory Method returns one product via subclassing, Abstract Factory returns several related products via composition — a single factory object exposes methods like createButton() and createCheckbox(), and a concrete factory implementation guarantees every product it returns belongs to the same family, so they're never accidentally mismatched.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Abstract Factory Pattern?

“Calling ____ and createCheckbox() on a DarkUIFactory always returns a matching dark button and dark checkbox — there's no code path where a dark button ends up paired with a light checkbox, because both came from the same factory instance.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.explanation: Calling createButton() and createCheckbox() on a DarkUIFactory always returns a matching dark button and dark checkbox — there's no code path where a dark button ends up paired with a light checkbox, because both came from the same factory instance.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Abstract Factory Pattern?

“Reaching for Abstract Factory when there's only ever one product to create is unnecessary — Factory Method, or even a plain ____, is simpler and sufficient.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.explanation: Reaching for Abstract Factory when there's only ever one product to create is unnecessary — Factory Method, or even a plain constructor, is simpler and sufficient.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Abstract Factory Pattern?

“Reach for Abstract ____ when you need a guaranteed-matching family of products, not just one product whose exact type varies.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--ab.explanation: Reach for Abstract Factory when you need a guaranteed-matching family of products, not just one product whose exact type varies.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Builder Pattern?

“Builder separates constructing a complex object from what that object ultimately looks like, letting you build it up step by step instead of via one unreadable ____ call.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.explanation: Builder separates constructing a complex object from what that object ultimately looks like, letting you build it up step by step instead of via one unreadable constructor call.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Builder Pattern?

“It fits objects with many optional fields, where a single constructor accepting every combination becomes an unreadable list of positional arguments (or worse, a family of overloaded ____ for every combination).”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.explanation: It fits objects with many optional fields, where a single constructor accepting every combination becomes an unreadable list of positional arguments (or worse, a family of overloaded constructors for every combination).

low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Builder Pattern?

“A ____ instead reads as new ____().setSize("large").setCrust("thin").addTopping("cheese").build() — every value is explicitly named at the call site, and optional fields can simply be left out.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.explanation: A PizzaBuilder instead reads as new PizzaBuilder().setSize("large").setCrust("thin").addTopping("cheese").build() — every value is explicitly named at the call site, and optional fields can simply be left out.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Builder Pattern?

“Reaching for ____ when an object only has two or three simple, always-required fields adds ceremony a plain constructor already handled clearly.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.explanation: Reaching for Builder when an object only has two or three simple, always-required fields adds ceremony a plain constructor already handled clearly.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Builder Pattern?

“A builder exposes one chained method per field, ending in a ____ call that assembles the final object once every desired field has been set.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--bu.explanation: A builder exposes one chained method per field, ending in a build() call that assembles the final object once every desired field has been set.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Prototype Pattern?

“____ creates new objects by cloning an existing instance rather than building from scratch — valuable when construction is expensive but a similar object already exists to copy.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.explanation: Prototype creates new objects by cloning an existing instance rather than building from scratch — valuable when construction is expensive but a similar object already exists to copy.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Prototype Pattern?

“A prototype object implements a ____ method that returns a copy of itself; instead of running the same expensive setup logic every time a similar object is needed, that setup runs once, and every subsequent instance comes from copying the already-configured prototype.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.explanation: A prototype object implements a clone() method that returns a copy of itself; instead of running the same expensive setup logic every time a similar object is needed, that setup runs once, and every subsequent instance comes from copying the already-configured prototype.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Prototype Pattern?

“A ____ template pre-loaded with textures and animation data that took real time to set up.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.explanation: A GameCharacter template pre-loaded with textures and animation data that took real time to set up.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Prototype Pattern?

“Forgetting the shallow-versus-deep-copy distinction is the pattern's ____ bug: a shallow clone that copies a reference to a mutable list, rather than the list itself, leaves the original and every clone silently sharing — and able to corrupt — the same underlying list.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.explanation: Forgetting the shallow-versus-deep-copy distinction is the pattern's signature bug: a shallow clone that copies a reference to a mutable list, rather than the list itself, leaves the original and every clone silently sharing — and able to corrupt — the same underlying list.

low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Prototype Pattern?

“Using Prototype when construction is already cheap adds a cloning ____ for savings that were never there.”
low-level-design/creational-patterns--pr.explanation: Using Prototype when construction is already cheap adds a cloning interface for savings that were never there.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Adapter Pattern?

“Adapter converts one class's interface into another interface a client expects, letting two incompatible ____ work together without modifying either one.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.explanation: Adapter converts one class's interface into another interface a client expects, letting two incompatible interfaces work together without modifying either one.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Adapter Pattern?

“An adapter implements the ____ the client already depends on, and internally holds a reference to the incompatible class, translating each call into whatever that class actually expects.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.explanation: An adapter implements the interface the client already depends on, and internally holds a reference to the incompatible class, translating each call into whatever that class actually expects.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Adapter Pattern?

“An application's PaymentProcessor interface expects ____, but a newly integrated third-party LegacyBillingSdk only exposes bill(amountInDollars, currency).”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.explanation: An application's PaymentProcessor interface expects charge(amountInCents), but a newly integrated third-party LegacyBillingSdk only exposes bill(amountInDollars, currency).

low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Adapter Pattern?

“Cramming too many unrelated ____ into one adapter turns it into a tangled mini-API of its own, rather than a focused translation layer.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.explanation: Cramming too many unrelated methods into one adapter turns it into a tangled mini-API of its own, rather than a focused translation layer.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Adapter Pattern?

“____'s whole job is translation between two interfaces that were never designed to match — keep it to just that, and fix interfaces you own instead of adapting around them.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--ad.explanation: Adapter's whole job is translation between two interfaces that were never designed to match — keep it to just that, and fix interfaces you own instead of adapting around them.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Decorator Pattern?

“Decorator attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically by wrapping it in another object that implements the same ____ — an alternative to subclassing that lets behaviors stack and combine at runtime.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.explanation: Decorator attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically by wrapping it in another object that implements the same interface — an alternative to subclassing that lets behaviors stack and combine at runtime.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Decorator Pattern?

“Each ____ implements the same interface as the object it wraps, and forwards calls to the wrapped object while adding its own behavior before or after.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.explanation: Each decorator implements the same interface as the object it wraps, and forwards calls to the wrapped object while adding its own behavior before or after.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Decorator Pattern?

“A Coffee interface with a cost() method: a MilkDecorator wraps any Coffee and adds milk's price on top of whatever the wrapped coffee already costs; a ____ can then wrap that combination and add mocha's price on top of that.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.explanation: A Coffee interface with a cost() method: a MilkDecorator wraps any Coffee and adds milk's price on top of whatever the wrapped coffee already costs; a MochaDecorator can then wrap that combination and add mocha's price on top of that.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Decorator Pattern?

“Subclassing for every combination of features — a CoffeeWithMilkAndMocha class, then ____ — explodes combinatorially as add-ons grow, which is exactly what Decorator avoids.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.explanation: Subclassing for every combination of features — a CoffeeWithMilkAndMocha class, then CoffeeWithMilkAndMochaAndWhip — explodes combinatorially as add-ons grow, which is exactly what Decorator avoids.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Decorator Pattern?

“Decorator trades a combinatorial explosion of ____ for a small set of composable wrappers — each one focused on adding exactly one behavior.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--de.explanation: Decorator trades a combinatorial explosion of subclasses for a small set of composable wrappers — each one focused on adding exactly one behavior.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Facade Pattern?

“Facade provides one simplified ____ in front of a complex subsystem of many interacting classes — without hiding that subsystem entirely from callers who genuinely need finer control.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.explanation: Facade provides one simplified interface in front of a complex subsystem of many interacting classes — without hiding that subsystem entirely from callers who genuinely need finer control.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Facade Pattern?

“The facade itself contains little logic of its own — its job is to know the right order to call the subsystem's existing ____ in, so most callers never have to learn that order themselves.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.explanation: The facade itself contains little logic of its own — its job is to know the right order to call the subsystem's existing classes in, so most callers never have to learn that order themselves.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Facade Pattern?

“A HomeTheaterFacade.____ method internally calls projector.on(), soundSystem.setVolume(), and streamingDevice.play() in the specific order that actually works.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.explanation: A HomeTheaterFacade.watchMovie() method internally calls projector.on(), soundSystem.setVolume(), and streamingDevice.play() in the specific order that actually works.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Facade Pattern?

“Letting the facade grow into a god-____ that reimplements subsystem logic itself, rather than just coordinating existing calls, defeats its purpose.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.explanation: Letting the facade grow into a god-object that reimplements subsystem logic itself, rather than just coordinating existing calls, defeats its purpose.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Facade Pattern?

“A ____'s value is in knowing the right order to call an existing subsystem — not in replacing that subsystem or being the only path to it.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--fa.explanation: A facade's value is in knowing the right order to call an existing subsystem — not in replacing that subsystem or being the only path to it.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Composite Pattern?

“Composite arranges objects into tree structures representing part-whole hierarchies, so a single object and a group of objects can be treated through the exact same ____.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.explanation: Composite arranges objects into tree structures representing part-whole hierarchies, so a single object and a group of objects can be treated through the exact same interface.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Composite Pattern?

“The composite's ____ typically delegates to each of its children — calling code never needs to check whether it's holding a leaf or a composite before calling the shared operation.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.explanation: The composite's implementation typically delegates to each of its children — calling code never needs to check whether it's holding a leaf or a composite before calling the shared operation.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Composite Pattern?

“A shared interface defines an operation that makes sense for both an individual “leaf” and a “____” that holds children of that same interface.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.explanation: A shared interface defines an operation that makes sense for both an individual “leaf” and a “composite” that holds children of that same interface.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Composite Pattern?

“Giving leaf nodes a meaningless implementation of composite-only operations, like ____ on a File that can never have children, is a sign the interface needs a cleaner split.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.explanation: Giving leaf nodes a meaningless implementation of composite-only operations, like addChild() on a File that can never have children, is a sign the interface needs a cleaner split.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Composite Pattern?

“Composite's payoff is treating one object and a whole subtree of ____ identically — the calling code stops needing to know which one it's holding.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--co.explanation: Composite's payoff is treating one object and a whole subtree of objects identically — the calling code stops needing to know which one it's holding.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Proxy Pattern?

“Proxy provides a stand-in object that controls access to another object — implementing the same ____, but able to add behavior like lazy loading, access control, or caching before forwarding the call along.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.explanation: Proxy provides a stand-in object that controls access to another object — implementing the same interface, but able to add behavior like lazy loading, access control, or caching before forwarding the call along.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Proxy Pattern?

“What the proxy adds is control: it might defer creating the real object until it's actually needed, check ____ before allowing a call through, or cache a result instead of forwarding every call.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.explanation: What the proxy adds is control: it might defer creating the real object until it's actually needed, check permissions before allowing a call through, or cache a result instead of forwarding every call.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Proxy Pattern?

“An ____ implements the same Image interface as a RealImage, but doesn't actually load the (expensive) image file from disk until display() is called on it for the first time.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.explanation: An ImageProxy implements the same Image interface as a RealImage, but doesn't actually load the (expensive) image file from disk until display() is called on it for the first time.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Proxy Pattern?

“Confusing Proxy with ____ is common since they look structurally similar in code — Proxy controls access to essentially the same object (often creating or gating it), while ____ adds genuinely new behavior to an object the client already fully has.”
low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.explanation: Confusing Proxy with Decorator is common since they look structurally similar in code — Proxy controls access to essentially the same object (often creating or gating it), while Decorator adds genuinely new behavior to an object the client already fully has.

low-level-design/structural-patterns--pr.prompt:
Which term completes this statement from Proxy Pattern?

“A proxy looks exactly like the real ____ to its callers, but controls when — or whether — the real, often expensive ____ actually gets involved.”
